To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genomic stability of lymphoblasts with germ-line p 53 mutation is not impaired in long-term culture.

1) EBV-immortalised lymphoblastoid cell lines from Li-Fraumenli syndrome patients with germ line p53 mutations do not show loss of p53 function during long term culture and 2) they maintain genomic stability during long-term culture.
p53 germ-line mutation in lymphocytes is not associated with genomic instability or loss of functional p53 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of the Li-Fraumenii Syndrome, a rare autosomic dominant inherited disease.
the study of the role of the p53 gene in the development of human cancers.
the study of the mechanisms that control genomic stability and the role played by p53 in these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p53 germ-line mutation is not sufficient for cancer development.
p53 germ-line mutation does not cause genomic instability in cultured lymphoblastoid cell lines, at least in the absence of other genetic or epigenetic factors.
the p53 germ line mutation does not affect the ability of lymphoblasts to maintain genomic stability in culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the germ-line mutant p53 lymphoblasts are not deficient in their ability to maintain genomic integrity, but rather that they maintain their genomic stability in a different manner than the fibroblasts.
germ-line p53 mutations do not necessarily lead to genomic instability in all cells, but only in some cell types, and that this is the basis of the selective tumorigenesis in Li-Fraumenis patients.
p53 is not essential to maintain genomic stability in lymphoblastic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p53 deficiency is not a sufficient condition to induce genomic instability.
the p53 gene has a very important role in maintaining genomic stability.
genomic instability in Li-Fraumenis syndrome is not due to the presence of a mutated p53 allele but rather due to the absence of the wild-type allele.
